msg.content: I’m inspecting the existing project structure first, then I’ll establish the minimal Android/Kotlin app skeleton and implement the game in a custom view so swipe input, rendering, timing, and restart behavior stay self-contained.

The repository is empty, so I’m creating a single-module Gradle Android project with no external runtime dependencies. The game will use a full-screen custom Kotlin `View`, which keeps the APK small and gives precise control over the board, score panel, swipe threshold, animation cadence, and game-over overlay.

msg.content: The project skeleton is in place. I’m adding the playable surface now: a responsive grid that sizes itself to the phone, a high-contrast dark visual system with mint snake and coral food, swipe direction locking to prevent accidental reversals, and a timer that accelerates as the score rises.

msg.content: The first implementation is complete, including the game loop and touch handling. I’m running the debug build now to catch configuration or Kotlin/API issues, then I’ll make any required compatibility fixes and rebuild until the APK is produced successfully.

The build reached Kotlin compilation and exposed one language-level issue: Kotlin does not allow the nested data class and enum declarations in this inner view class. I’m moving those two simple types to file scope; no gameplay behavior changes are needed.
